why.rb_lev_2.m_nFieldsCount: 3.9 (owner: a review of the levels of Roadblocks). 1 → 2 fields in a Hard game, 7500 points each (data/roadblocks_levels.json), so the game is still worth 15000 and a lost ball still costs 2000. With one field a Hard game was often shorter than a Medium one with its two fields: by the careful explorer of tools/analysis/roadblocks_review.mjs a third of the Hard fields took fewer rolls than an average Medium game, and the real logs (docs/analytics/players-2026-11.md) agree. Together with the re-sorted pools (tools/roadblocks_resort.mjs: Medium — the 12 originals with a 3–8 roll solution that are not trap fields; Hard — the other 28, a solution of 9 rolls or more or a short trap field) a game takes about 9 rolls of the shortest way on Easy, 9–13 on Medium and 18–57 on Hard. The first round deals the fields from the simpler to the harder ones; the ten Hard games of the bar end with the four longest mazes. The thresholds stay: at most one lost ball on Easy, none on Medium and Hard. In the real logs careful players lose no balls at all, so the model's pass rates quoted below (novice 17 %, average 60 % on Medium) are too low for people; the log of games now keeps the fields of a game with their seconds and rolls (play.f1…, s1…, r1…) to sort the pools by real data later.
why.MG_road_blocks_hard.level_up_param: 3.7 (owner: on Medium and Hard no ball may be lost). up 13000 → 15000 = the field without a lost ball (15000 − 2000 per ball): average 22 % (was 36 %; the Hard target is 20–30 %), strong 71 % (was 75 %), novice 4 %; games for the 10 steps (median): average 45, strong 14. Weak games (under 6000 = five balls lost): average 9 %, novice 52 %. Mean scores of the average player rise 5100 → 8820 → 10830, so the harder level pays more. Steps 3 / 5 / 10 like every game.
why.MG_road_blocks_easy.level_up_param: v3.3 (owner: easy had 6 steps of big hard fields, the pools were not sorted by difficulty — easy held fields of 37 and 51 rolls, hard a field of 3). The fields are re-sorted (tools/roadblocks_resort.mjs, metrics: tools/analysis/roadblocks_fields.mjs): easy — 12 new small fields 9×11 with one exit and a 2–4 roll solution, 3 per game; medium — the 15 easier original fields (3–12 rolls), 2 per game; hard — the other 25 (5–51 rolls), 1 per game. Steps 3 / 5 / 10 like every game. Easy: up 4100 = at most one lost ball in the three fields (5100 − 1000 per ball): novice 90 %, average and strong 100 % of games (model players of tools/analysis/train_balance_roadblocks.mjs). Unlock (4th number): level-ups needed to open the game. v3.3 (owner: the last games opened too slowly): 1, 2, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11, 13, 15 instead of 1, 2, 3, 6, 8, 11, 14, 16, 18 — the average model player opens all 12 games in 23–30 trainings instead of 30–42 (tools/analysis/unlock_pace.py). 3.12.4 (owner: Easy is won often by a beginner, but not every time): up 4100 → 5100, no lost ball in the three fields, the rule of Medium and Hard (the game has no time penalty, so a step is a clean result). Novice 90 → 62 % of the games (target 60–75 %), average and strong 100 %. Careful players lose no ball on these 2–4 roll fields, so for them nothing changes.
why.MG_road_blocks_med.level_up_param: 3.7 (owner: Roadblocks has no time penalty, so on Medium and Hard a step must mean that no ball is lost; 3.6 had lowered it to 8000 = one lost ball). up 10000 = both fields without a lost ball (10000 − 2000 per ball): novice 17 %, average 60 %, strong 96 %; games for the 5 steps (median): novice 28, average 8. Weak games (under 4000 = four balls lost): average 1 %, novice 41 %. The fields are those of 3.3 (tools/roadblocks_resort.mjs, tools/analysis/roadblocks_fields.mjs): easy — 12 small fields 9×11 with one exit and a 2–4 roll solution, 3 per game; medium — the 15 easier original fields (3–12 rolls), 2 per game; hard — the other 25 (5–51 rolls), 1 per game. Easy stays at 4100 = at most one lost ball in the three fields (novice 90 %, average 100 %).
